However the change set removes or dilutes several quality oracles rather than preserving their semantics under simpler behavior, and the supplied current facts do not bind the acceptance criteria they claim to cover. AC-12 requires that every tracked test carry exactly one disposition, yet the disposition ledger, its generator, and its contract test are all deleted with no replacement enumerator. tools/architecture/inventory.mjs now unconditionally requires docs/architecture/deletions-proof.json under --check, but that artifact appears in neither the 143-file diff nor the inventory ledger, so the gate the diff adds cannot pass and AC-06's per-deletion proof is unverifiable from the frozen bundle. The AC-11 runner-drift fail-closed check is deleted and its test inverted to expect success. The claimed-vs-actual diff equality check is now skipped whenever the claim list is empty, which prose actual_changes reliably produces. These are oracle removals on the safety side of the ledger, so the simplification is not yet demonstrably quality-preserving.","findings":[{"severity":"blocking","path":"tools/architecture/inventory.mjs","line":null,"issue":"validateDeletionProof() requires docs/architecture/deletions-proof.json (schema workflowhub-deletions-proof.v1, 40-hex baseline commit/tree, per-entry absent===true, consumer_zero_ref into complexity-baseline.json#/hard_gates/dedicated_recovery_state, an existing replacement_oracle, and user_confirmation.ref === docs/architecture/legacy-import-proof.json with confirmation.user_confirmed === true), and main() pushes its errors on every --check run.
